construct: MYO5B encodes myosin Vb, an actin-based motor/tether that cooperates with Rab8/Rab11 recycling pathways to deliver and recycle apical cargo in polarized enterocytes. Loss disrupts apical membrane trafficking and brush-border protein localization, causing severe congenital diarrhea and characteristic microvillus inclusions.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: Neonatal intractable diarrhea, absent brush border, microvillus inclusions, and biallelic MYO5B loss identify MVID from disrupted myosin-Vb/Rab-dependent apical recycling and cargo delivery in enterocytes.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: Presynaptic SNARE release, LDL endocytosis, neuronal dynein transport, and COPII ER export are genuine trafficking pathways but do not explain the polarized enterocyte apical-recycling defect produced by MYO5B loss.
adversarial_second_pass.expert_reviewer_reversal: The genotype and pathognomonic histology fix both the disease and the relevant trafficking compartment, preventing a generic-vesicle-transport alternative.
